summary: bcore-bravo-eslint-config ships a postinstall + import-time dropper that fetches and executes a remote binary
details: The package's postinstall hook runs setup.js, which assembles destination hostnames at runtime from split string arrays (joined with.join('')) to hide oob-worker.cfNN-XXX.workers.dev and *.dl.well1.site, with a DNS-TXT covert-channel fallback that reassembles base64 chunks from resolveTxt responses into an executable payload. The downloaded binary is written to /var/tmp or the Windows TEMP directory under cover-story names such as dotnet_diag_<rand>.exe and.cache_<rand>, chmod 0755 on POSIX, and detached-launched via execSync/child_process (setup.js line 70+ uses require('child_process') and execSync('powershell...')). index.js unconditionally require()s./setup at module load, so the same dropper fires on library import as well as on npm install, defeating --ignore-scripts. The fetched bytes are not pinned, not hashed, and delivered from anonymous Cloudflare Workers subdomains that do not match any legitimate eslint-config publisher. An eslint config package has no legitimate need to download and execute a native binary.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
